sections.h2: Where is the Marinette County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The Marinette County Register of Deeds is at 1926 Hall Ave, Marinette, WI 54143. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. The main phone number is 715-732-7551 and the fax is 715-732-7556. Packages sent by FedEx or UPS go to a separate address, 1925 Ella Court, Marinette, WI 54143.

The office describes its job as being the official county repository for real estate instruments and vital records, with archival storage and convenient access to them. It also collects and accounts for fees under Wisconsin statutes. For a house sale, that means the deed, any mortgage payoff paperwork and the transfer return all pass through this counter.

sections.h2: What is Marinette County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Marinette County is large and thinly settled. It covers 1,550 square miles, of which 1,399 are land and 151 (9.7 percent) are water, making it the third largest Wisconsin county by land area and the fifth largest in total area. Part of its edge touches Lake Michigan. The Peshtigo and Menominee rivers, many lakes and forests, and a large snowmobile trail network draw visitors, and Dave's Falls near Amberg is one of the county's waterfalls. The county's own website calls Marinette County the Waterfalls Capital of Wisconsin.

The Census Bureau counted 41,872 people in 2020 and estimated 42,574 for July 2025, up 1.7 percent. The 2020 census showed 29,189 housing units and a vacancy figure of 35.8 percent. By comparison, the same census page for Marathon County shows 5.5 percent and the one for Milwaukee County shows 7.2 percent. About 60.8 percent of residents lived in rural areas.

  • Median age: 49.3 years (2020 census), with 28.3 percent of residents 65 or older.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 81.6 percent (2020 to 2024).
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $158,600.
  • Median gross rent: $795 a month.
  • Median household income: $63,809.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 215.

The city of Marinette is the county seat, and the county belongs to the Marinette, WI to MI Micropolitan Statistical Area. Crivitz Municipal Airport serves the county. Workers face a mean commute of 21.1 minutes, and the Census Bureau puts the poverty rate at 11.8 percent.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Marinette County?
sections.html:
The office follows Wisconsin's statutory fees. Recording a document is $30, and all fees are payable in advance by the person asking for the service under Wis. Stat. 59.43(2g). Copies are $2 for the first page and $1 per added page, plus $1 to certify one. The county's own fee page, titled User Fees, sits under the Register of Deeds menu, and the office can tell you about any other charge.

Recording a deed, mortgage or other document$30Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag)

Copy of a recorded document$2 first page, $1 each added pageWis. Stat. 59.43(2)(b)

sections.h2: What does the Marinette County office do with a deed once it arrives?
sections.html:
State law spells out the register's duties in Wis. Stat. 59.43(1c). They include the following:

  • Record each document in the order it is received.
  • Stamp it with the date, hour and minute of recording, which is prima facie evidence of when it was recorded.
  • Give it a unique number that follows the number of the previous document in its series.
  • Keep the originals, images and indexes permanently.
  • Note on a conveyance the transfer fee paid, or cite the reason it is exempt.
  • Deliver the recorded document to the person you name, once you provide adequate postage.

The endorsement matters when two documents reach the same property close together, such as a deed and a mortgage. A seller with a closing date should get the deed to the office early, since the stamp records the order in which documents arrived.

sections.h2: How does the transfer fee work on a Marinette County sale?
sections.html:
The seller owes 30 cents for each $100 of value, or fraction of $100, on a conveyance that is not exempt. On a $158,600 sale, about the county median home value, the fee comes to about $476. For a land contract the value is the total principal the buyer agrees to pay, and for a gift or exchange it is the estimated open market price.

Buyer and seller must both sign a transfer return. Since July 1, 2009 the state has required filing it electronically unless the Department of Revenue waives that for hardship, and the county site lists Wisconsin Real Estate Transfer Returns on the Register of Deeds menu. Completed returns and the fees go to the county treasurer monthly by the 15th, and 20 percent of the money stays with the county. A city, village, town or county cannot add its own fee to a conveyance that the state fee exempts.

sections.h2: Which Marinette County transfers owe no state fee?
sections.html:
Wis. Stat. 77.25 lists the exempt conveyances. A few that matter for private owners are these:

  • A transfer by will, descent or survivorship.
  • A deed from a trustee to a beneficiary, or between agent and principal, without actual consideration.
  • A transfer between parent and child, or grandparent and grandchild, for nominal or no consideration.
  • A conveyance made only to give or release security for a debt.
  • A deed on foreclosure, or in place of it, to the mortgage holder or the land contract seller.
  • A deed that completes a land contract when the proper fee was paid on the contract.

Exemptions are read narrowly, so a transfer that is close to one of these but not squarely inside it may still owe the fee. Ask a Wisconsin attorney if your situation is unclear.

sections.h2: Can I record electronically or search Marinette County records online?
sections.html:
Yes to both. The county lists two electronic recording services: CSC (Corporation Services Corp), reachable at 866-403-5272, and Simplifile at 800-460-5657. Online, LandShark provides access to documents recorded in the Marinette County Register of Deeds office from 1990 forward. You can register and view the index at no charge. The site offers one option for daily users, such as title firms that need to view and buy images, and another for occasional users.

The county warns that someone without a real estate background may do better to visit the office for help locating a document.

faqs.q: What are the hours of the Marinette County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. It is at 1926 Hall Ave, Marinette, WI 54143, and the phone number is 715-732-7551. Packages from FedEx or UPS go to 1925 Ella Court.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Marinette County?
faqs.a: Recording costs $30 under Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag), payable in advance. A state transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value also applies unless the transfer is exempt. Copies are $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page.

faqs.q: Does Marinette County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes. The county lists CSC (866-403-5272) and Simplifile (800-460-5657) as electronic recording providers. Ask whoever is handling your closing whether they will submit the deed through one of them.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer fee when I sell a house in Marinette County?
faqs.a: The seller, who is called the grantor in the statute. Wis. Stat. 77.22 puts the fee on the grantor, and the register collects it when the deed is submitted. Both buyer and seller sign the electronic transfer return.

faqs.q: Are Marinette County records available online?
faqs.a: Yes. LandShark offers documents recorded from 1990 forward, and registering and viewing the index is free. The daily-user option is built for firms that view and buy images. For anything older than 1990, ask the Register of Deeds at 715-732-7551 how to get a copy.
